02

A Friday on the Avenue

Someone drives past the sign
and wants to eat there.

Eight o'clock on a Friday. Four people in a car on St. Charles, they see the neon, and somebody pulls out a phone to check if there is a table.

01

They search on the phone

They type the name into Google, or land on a beer directory while they are still driving over.

02

They tap the official site

BeerMenus still lists tacosandbeer.org as your website. It is the first link they see.

03

The domain is dead

It expired in September 2018. Today it is parked and serving somebody else's ads. Every visit that lands there earns money for another person.

04

So they call instead

Eight o'clock on a Friday. The phone is behind the bar and nobody can get to it.

The domain and the email address can both be checked live, in front of you, in under a minute.

03

What never reached you

Seven years of email
that never
got to you.

info@tacosandbeer.org was the address for catering, for private events, and for musicians asking to play. It lives on the same domain that expired.

Nobody knows how many birthdays, rehearsal dinners and catering quotes were written to that address since 2018. What is certain is that none of them arrived, and that the person who wrote assumed you did not care to answer.

Verified

$360 to $420

Average check for a group or a catering order, against roughly $40 for a takeout order.
Verified

You have done it before

You sold VIP balcony tickets for Mardi Gras in 2016. Today there is nowhere to sell them.
04

The turn

Everything a restaurant
gets judged on,
you already have.

Fourteen years. Three dining rooms. Around 1,125 people who took the time to sit down and write about you. The stretch that breaks is the one between wanting to come in and sitting down.

Today that stretch runs through directories you do not control, a domain that stopped being yours in 2018, and a phone that rings at the worst moment of the shift. That is what we build, and that is what we keep running.

How the line works

Three steps, and none of them
pulls anybody off the floor.

01

They join from wherever they are

Name, phone, how many. From the car, from the house, from the sidewalk out front.

02

They show up on your screen

Right away, with how long they have waited and which location. Nothing to install.

03

They get a text when the table is ready

No shouting a name across the room, no answering the phone in the middle of a rush.

A walk-in taqueria runs on the line. That is what we built, and that is why there is no calendar to keep or table times to hold.

09

What you are known for

Taco Tuesday gets
a room of its own.

The rest of the week it counts down. On Tuesday the whole site lights up and single tacos show up struck through at a dollar on the menu.

And here is how we handle your data. The dollar price is only promised in Slidell, which is the one location where it is confirmed with a photograph from the restaurant itself. In Hammond it only shows up in reviews, and in New Orleans it does not show up at all, so there the site invites people to ask. If we cannot show you where a number came from, the site does not print it.

tacosandbeer.com/#tuesday

12

Before you sign with anyone

Five questions worth asking.
Ours are answered on this page.

Question 01

What does it cost, and can I see the number before a sales call?

We checked. The platform behind the site you sent us does not publish a price anywhere. You book a demo first. Our numbers are in this document, before you meet anybody.
Question 02

What happens the day I want to leave?

Ask about contract length and what cancelling costs. With us the domain and the content stay in the name of Tacos and Beer, LLC, in an account you control. If you leave, the site is still yours.
Question 03

How fast does it load on a phone?

Measured below. This is the number that moves your Google Maps ranking and the number of people who wait for the page instead of closing it.
Question 04

Can Google read my menu?

On the site you sent, the menus are buttons that lead somewhere else. Google has nothing to read. Every dish on your site is written into the page with structured data, so someone searching for al pastor in New Orleans can land on you.
Question 05

Who answers when I need a change on a Friday?

A name and a response time, in writing. Not a support address.
Verified

We are a new firm. That is why this costs less than the platforms and why you are seeing the whole site built before you have paid anything.

Why it holds this time

For five years
the site did its job.
Then it was gone.

A renewal notice went out to an inbox nobody was reading anymore. Nothing broke loudly. One season the site was there and the next it was parked, and seven years went by before anyone counted the cost. Somebody has to be watching. That is the monthly work.

Every month

It stays up

Hosting, certificate, backups, monitoring and renewal alerts. The domain stays in the name of Tacos and Beer, LLC, in an account you control.
Every month

It stays current

Menu changes, prices, hours and seasonal events. And your site, your Google listing and the ordering apps saying the same thing.
Every month

It gets measured

A plain report: how many people came, what they looked for, how many joined the line, and how many groups wrote in.

Pricing is prepared separately, once the scope is confirmed in the meeting.
